patch_description: The current force-based relaxation keeps all points on a unit sphere, which caps the achievable ratio: the diameter of the configuration stays 2 while the best packing of 14 points on a sphere only reaches dmin ≈ 0.59, giving ratio² ≈ 0.09 at best, far from the reference 0.24. The true optimum of dmin/dmax is scale/rotation/translation invariant and generally does NOT lie on a sphere (the optimal configuration can have a smaller diameter relative to its minimum separation). So instead of a sphere-constrained relaxation, I directly optimize a smooth approximation of the target ratio (dmin/dmax)² over freely moving points, using L-BFGS with many random restarts. Smooth softmin/softmax over pairwise distances give useful gradients; after each run the exact ratio is computed and the best configuration kept. Random restarts make it robust; fixed seeds keep it deterministic. Points are normalized (centered, max coordinate scaled) at the end only as a convenience — this doesn't affect the score.
